## 1. Executive Summary

**Biggest strengths (what is already in place)**
- **The technical schema foundation already exists.** `lib/schema.ts` ships typed builders for Organization (`["FinancialService","LocalBusiness"]` with `@id` graph, NAP, geo, areaServed, openingHours, makesOffer, founder, knowsAbout), WebSite, Person (with correct LLQP `hasCredential`), Service, FAQPage, Breadcrumb and Article — plus a reusable `<JsonLd>` component and `globalGraph()` wired into `app/layout.tsx`.
- **Clean Next.js 14 App Router base:** single-source `siteConfig`, `metadataBase`, dynamic `opengraph-image.tsx`, `sitemap.ts`, `robots.ts`, `en_CA` OG locale, an MDX blog pipeline, 8 existing blog posts, 6 services, a team directory, and 9 `/tools/*` calculators.
- **A genuine, hard-to-replicate local + niche moat:** real Olds/Sundre/Red Deer testimonial clients, authentic community ties (Olds Grizzlys, BGC Olds & Area, 4-H Canada, MVESS), an agricultural service area, and a fiduciary/fee-only positioning that the bank/branch competitors (ATB, Desjardins, Servus, IG, Co-operators, Manulife) structurally cannot claim.

**The core problem:** the schema builders are **dead code** — only `globalGraph()` (Organization + WebSite) is emitted. Service, team, FAQ and blog pages ship without their structured data; the blog re-rolls an inferior inline `BlogPosting`. Metadata is generic and **non-local** (never mentions Olds/Alberta). `siteConfig.sameAs` is empty, so AI engines can't resolve the entity. There is **no Google Business Profile foundation**, no citations, no local landing pages, and the `/faq` copy makes two **YMYL accuracy errors** ("fee-only fiduciary" / "registered investment advisor") that contradict the LLQP-only reality.

**Top 5 highest-impact priorities**
1. **Claim + fully optimize the Google Business Profile** and build NAP-consistent Canadian citations. For a single-location firm in a ~9,300-person market, GBP is the #1 local ranking factor and (per Yext's 2025 study) directory listings are a primary AI-citation source for financial services.
2. **Wire up the existing schema builders** (FAQPage on `/faq`, Service + Breadcrumb on services, Person + Breadcrumb on team, richer Article + named Person author on blog) — emitted from server-side `layout.tsx` files. Highest-leverage on-page win, mostly plumbing.
3. **Fix the two YMYL copy contradictions** on `/faq` *before* amplifying them with schema, and **populate `siteConfig.sameAs`** with the real GBP/Facebook/LinkedIn URLs once verified.
4. **Localize all metadata** (titles/descriptions/OG) with "Olds, Alberta" / "central Alberta" and build **3–5 genuinely differentiated local landing pages** (Olds primary, then Sundre/Didsbury/Red Deer) using real local testimonials — no thin doorway pages.
5. **Publish a pillar-and-cluster content program** focused on **winnable** Alberta-specific + conversational/AEO long-tail (farm succession, Alberta tax brackets, CPP/OAS timing, "do I need an advisor", fee-only explainer) — not national head terms owned by Wealthsimple and the banks.

**Verdict:** Birchtree is *technically* further along than a typical small-firm site but is leaving nearly all of its local and AI-search value unrealized. The work is high-ROI and low-risk: most of the highest-impact moves are **off-page (GBP/citations/reviews/sponsor links)** or **plumbing existing code**, not green-field development. Execute the quick wins this week and the local + content investments this quarter to own "financial advisor Olds / central Alberta" and the conversational money-questions the banks and robo-advisors leave un-localized.

## 3. Local SEO Action List

**A. Google Business Profile (the #1 local lever — off-page, no code)**
- **Claim + verify** the listing for `4914 50 Ave, Olds, AB T4H 1P5` (video verification is now standard in Canada). Have **LLQP licensing details ready** — financial-advisor categories can trigger verification.
- **Primary category:** `Financial Planner`. **Secondary:** `Financial Consultant`, `Insurance Agency`, `Investment Service`.
- Fill **every** field: exact NAP, hours (Mon–Fri 9–5 MST), website, appointment link, full "from the business" description naming **Olds + central Alberta + the 6 services**, and all **6 services** with descriptions in the Services section.
- **Ongoing:** publish **Posts** ≥ monthly (RRSP/TFSA deadlines, sponsorship news, blog reshares), seed + answer the **Q&A** section ("Do you serve Sundre/Red Deer?"), upload genuine **geotagged photos** of the 4914 50 Ave office exterior/interior, team, and community events.
- Once live, copy the GBP URL into `siteConfig.sameAs` and ensure the schema `hasMap` points to it.

**B. NAP consistency (the most common local-SEO mistake)**
- Maintain **one canonical NAP master record** (a spreadsheet): `Birchtree Financial / 4914 50 Ave, Olds, AB T4H 1P5 / (403) 556-7777 / https://birchtreefinancial.ca / melissa.birch@birchtreefinancial.ca`. Use the **contact-page address verbatim** as the source of truth and copy it byte-identically everywhere (site footer, schema, GBP, every citation).

**C. Citations / directories (build manually, identical NAP)**
- **Tier 1 (highest authority):** Apple Business Connect (Apple Maps/Siri), Bing Places, Facebook Business Page, YellowPages.ca, Yelp.ca, Foursquare.
- **Tier 2 (Canada-specific):** n49, Cylex.ca, HotFrog.ca, Brownbook, Opendi.ca, ProfileCanada, CanadaOne, Canada411, FoundLocally, iBegin.
- **Finance-relevant:** Better Business Bureau (BBB).
- Do these **manually** (not bulk-submit) to avoid sloppy data.

**D. Reviews (compliant, non-cherry-picked routine)**
- Generate the GBP "review us" short-link; embed it in a post-meeting email template. After onboarding, annual reviews, or plan delivery, email **every** client on a CRM rotation — not just happy ones.
- **Conduct rules (Canadian provincial insurance-council / CIRO standards — same effect as the US SEC Marketing Rule):** genuine reviews only, no incentives, no scripting/pressure, no selective solicitation, no curating responses to look like control. Aim for a steady drip, not a one-time burst.

**E. Local backlinks from real sponsorships (authentic, hard to replicate)**
- Confirm each sponsorship is current, then email each webmaster requesting a **logo + link** on the sponsors/partners page: **Olds Grizzlys** (Jr A hockey), **BGC Olds & Area**, **4-H Canada**, **MVESS** shelter.
- **Join the Olds & District Chamber of Commerce** (oldsalberta.com, 403-556-7070) for a Chamber Market member-directory listing/citation.
- Pursue **InvestOlds.ca** and local Olds news/event sites. Local `.ca` sponsorship links carry strong geographic relevance.

**F. Local landing pages (quality over quantity — doorway-safe)**
- Build **3–5** genuinely differentiated pages (Olds primary, then Sundre/Didsbury/Innisfail/Red Deer) using **real per-town testimonials** (Olds/Sundre/Red Deer clients already exist), local context, and town-specific FAQs. **Never** mass-produce near-duplicate town-swap pages (Google penalizes doorway pages). Each gets LocalBusiness/FinancialService schema + internal links from home/services.

**G. Audits**
- Quarterly NAP-consistency + duplicate-listing audit against the master spreadsheet (the footer email drifted once in commit `a7c3dec` — exactly the kind of drift to catch). Suppress/merge any duplicate GBP listings via Google support.

## 4. AI / Answer-Engine Optimization (AEO/GEO) Action List

**A. Fix YMYL accuracy first (trust gate — do before amplifying with schema)**
- In `app/faq/page.tsx`, replace "**registered investment advisor … held to a fiduciary standard**" and "**fee-only fiduciary**" with reality-matching copy, e.g.: *"We act in a fiduciary-minded, client-first way; our advisors hold the Life License Qualification Program (LLQP) license and we are a registered financial advisory firm in Canada. We are compensated through the company, not by direct fees to you."* Confirm exact wording with Melissa Birch. Keep terminology consistent across `/faq`, `/about`, `/services`. **Never** assert CFP/CFA. AI engines penalize YMYL inconsistency.

**B. Entity resolution — populate `sameAs`**
- `siteConfig.sameAs` is `[]`, so engines get zero corroborating identity signals. Add **verified** URLs only: claimed Google Business Profile, Facebook page, LinkedIn company page (Instagram if active). `organizationSchema()` auto-emits them once non-empty. Per Yext's 6.8M-citation study, 88% of financial-services AI citations come from brand-managed sources — these owned profiles directly feed citations. (Long-horizon: a **Wikidata** item once 2–3 independent corroborating references exist — do not fabricate references.)

**C. Answer-first formatting (GEO)**
- On `/services/[slug]`, `/faq`, `/why-you-need-a-will`, and every new article: convert H2/H3 headings into the **exact questions** users ask AI; open each section with a **40–60 word direct answer capsule** before elaborating; include one concrete Canadian number with an inline CRA/canada.ca link per ~150–200 words (**VERIFY/CRA**); use bulleted/numbered lists and comparison tables liberally (highly cited formats). Adding statistics/citable data measurably lifts AI visibility.

**D. FAQ + entity schema (builders already exist — wire them up)**
- Emit `faqSchema()` from `app/faq/layout.tsx` (server component) so it's in initial HTML; marked-up answer text must **exactly match** visible accordion text. Note: Google removed FAQ *rich results* (May 2026) — keep FAQPage purely as an **AEO/AI-citation signal** (ChatGPT/Perplexity/AI Overviews still extract it; FAQPage pages cite at materially higher rates). Add small FAQ blocks at the bottom of key service/blog pages and town pages.

**E. Author E-E-A-T on blog**
- Switch `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` from the inline `BlogPosting` to `articleSchema()`, set `author` to a **named Person** referencing `${url}/team/melissa-birch#person` (publisher stays `#organization`), add a real `dateModified` and a visible byline + "Last updated" date (Perplexity/AI Overviews weight freshness). Author bio should state LLQP licensing — never CFP/CFA.

**F. AI-crawler robots policy (with trade-offs)**
- In `app/robots.ts`, keep `{ userAgent:'*', allow:'/', disallow:['/admin/','/api/'] }` and add **explicit allow** rules for citation bots: `OAI-SearchBot`, `ChatGPT-User`, `ClaudeBot`, `Claude-SearchBot`, `PerplexityBot`, `Perplexity-User`, `Google-Extended`, `GPTBot`. Each blocked bot is estimated to cost ~18–34% of potential citations on that engine; ~27% of sites accidentally block them at the CDN/WAF layer — **verify on Vercel** with `curl -A 'OAI-SearchBot' https://birchtreefinancial.ca` and confirm a 200.
- **Trade-off / owner decision:** allowing training crawlers (`GPTBot`, `Google-Extended`) trades content training for long-term brand familiarity in models. **Recommended here** — the goal is visibility, not content protection.

**G. llms.txt (low priority, cheap insurance)**
- No major vendor acts on it today and studies show no traffic impact, but it's near-zero effort. Add `/public/llms.txt` (or `app/llms.txt/route.ts` returning `text/plain`): `# Birchtree Financial` + one-line summary + link sections (Core pages, Helpful answers, Tools). Optional `llms-full.txt` with expanded service/FAQ text.

**H. Become the primary citable source**
- Publish original, **Alberta-specific, current-year** answer content national sites won't localize (2026 limits **VERIFY/CRA**, CPP/OAS timing for Albertans, RRSP-vs-TFSA decision tables, fee-only/fiduciary explainer). Brand-owned authoritative answer pages dominate finance AI citations.

### 5.2 Enrich the existing Organization node (`organizationSchema()`)
- **Fix `priceRange`:** it's currently the string `"Free initial consultation"` — `priceRange` expects a symbolic value. Set `priceRange:'$$'` (or omit) and move "Free initial consultation" into a dedicated `Offer`/`description`.
- Make `logo` a full `ImageObject` (width/height); add a real office `image` (not the 512px icon). Add `foundingDate` if known, `slogan`, optionally `numberOfEmployees`.
- Add `sameAs[]` (Section 4B) once verified. Keep NAP byte-identical to GBP.

### 5.3 Next.js metadata + file fixes
- **Localize all metadata:** rewrite root + per-page `layout.tsx` `title`/`description`/`keywords`/`openGraph` to include "Olds, Alberta" / "central Alberta" and state fee/fiduciary language plainly. E.g. home `Financial Advisor in Olds, Alberta | Birchtree Financial`; geo-tag about/team/contact/services. Keep titles < ~60 chars, descriptions ~150–160. Template `%s | Birchtree Financial` is fine.
- **Canonicals:** `alternates.canonical` is only on root/`/blog`/`/blog/[slug]`. Add it to **every** layout (relative path, `metadataBase` already set): `app/services/[service]/layout.tsx` → `/services/${slug}`; `app/team/[slug]/layout.tsx` → `/team/${slug}`; plus `/services`, `/team`, `/about`, `/contact`, `/faq`, `/tools/*`, `/resources`.
- **Locale:** set `<html lang="en-CA">` in `app/layout.tsx`; optionally `alternates.languages:{'en-CA':'/'}` + `x-default`. Don't fabricate fr-CA alternates.
- **OG images:** keep the global `opengraph-image.tsx` (cascades to all routes). Add `app/blog/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx` (next/og `ImageResponse`, render title/author/date). Add a `twitter-image.tsx` or rely on Next's OG→Twitter mapping. Keep OG ≤ 8MB / Twitter ≤ 5MB.
- **Sitemap:** drive `app/sitemap.ts` entries from `siteConfig.services`/`team` + the blog index (avoid hardcoded-list drift); use **real** `lastModified` (git mtime or `post.updatedAt`) instead of `new Date()` on every build. Add the new town/landing/glossary URLs. Confirm submission in Google Search Console.
- **Robots:** see Section 4F (explicit AI-bot allow rules + Vercel WAF check).

### 5.4 Hardening & quality (lower priority)
- **XSS:** `components/seo/JsonLd.tsx` uses `JSON.stringify` + `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; `JSON.stringify` doesn't escape `<`. Apply Next's documented mitigation: `.replace(/</g,'\\u003c')`. Removes a real injection vector as content becomes CMS-driven.
- **Typing:** add `schema-dts` to `lib/schema.ts` builders (`WithContext<FinancialService>`, etc.) to catch misspelled properties (e.g. `areaServed`) at build time.
- **Core Web Vitals:** give the LCP hero `priority` + explicit width/height (CLS→0) and don't animate it; keep framer-motion below the fold + viewport-gated, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; convert static `"use client"` marketing pages (`services/[service]`, `team/[slug]`, `faq`) to **server components** where possible (better LCP, crawlability, lets JSON-LD live on the page); add `optimizePackageImports` for `framer-motion`/`recharts` and lazy-load chart/tool pages via `next/dynamic`. Target LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1.

### Seasonal calendar (publish ~4–6 weeks before peak; refresh annually)
- **Jan–Feb (RRSP season):** "RRSP Season Checklist" + RRSP/TFSA-vs-RRSP live by **early January**; deadline **March 2, 2026** for 2025 tax year (**VERIFY/CRA**).
- **Mar–Apr (tax season):** Alberta tax brackets, year-round tax-optimization, reduce-taxes-in-retirement; filing deadline ~April 30 (**VERIFY/CRA**).
- **Spring:** FHSA / first-home content.
- **Jun–Jul:** mid-year portfolio + insurance reviews.
- **Oct–Dec (year-end):** tax-loss selling, TFSA top-up, charitable giving, RESP year-end; "Year-End Tax Planning Checklist."
- **Every January:** the moment CRA confirms new limits, update **all** contribution-limit/bracket figures so the site is never the stale result.
